documents.unit: Office of the Provost (Provost-appointed AI Working Group)
documents.title: A Report on AI and the UAB Community
documents.date_or_term: undated in fetch; current as linked (accessed 2026-10-25); report dated June 29, 2023
documents.stance_why: The report states 'UAB does not dictate that teachers shall require or prohibit the use of generative AI' and tells teachers to set course-level decisions and put them in the syllabus. It also gives sample statements that prohibit, allow with attribution, or encourage AI. It sets no stance itself and offers templates, so it delegates.
documents.summary: A 2023 provost working-group report surveying AI capabilities, risks and equity issues, then recommending that teachers decide AI use per course and state it in the syllabus. It sets integrity rules (undisclosed AI is misconduct), recommends tool vetting, legal review and training, and supplies sample syllabus statements.

units.why: It says UAB 'does not dictate that teachers shall require or prohibit' generative AI: no university stance, the decision rests with teachers, so P04.

units.why: It grounds the delegation in academic freedom, saying teachers have 'substantial latitude'. This explains the instructor-level decision, so P04 with a note.

units.fit_note: Gives the academic-freedom justification for instructor discretion rather than the delegation itself.

units.why: It says 'All course requirements must adhere to UAB policies as well as the UAB Academic Integrity Code', binding course rules to existing policy, P77.
units.anchor: All course requirements must adhere to UAB policies as well as the UAB Academic Integrity

units.why: Teachers are 'encouraged' to make decisions 'appropriate for their specific content and student learning objectives', so choices follow learning objectives, P83.

units.why: Decisions 'should be clearly outlined in the course syllabus and communicated to students', a syllabus-statement duty, P09.

units.why: Teachers are empowered to 'Insist on academic integrity'. It is an empowerment statement tied to honesty, so P95 with a note.
units.anchor: Insist on academic integrity.
units.fit_note: An empowerment statement rather than a reasoned justification.

units.why: Teachers may 'Ensure AI cannot be used as a proxy to pass a university course', meaning AI must not stand in for the student's thinking; nearest is P32.
units.anchor: Ensure AI cannot be used as a proxy to pass a university course.

units.anchor: Encourage openness and sharing of experiences with emerging technologies.

units.why: Teachers may 'Require complete and accurate documentation of how AI is employed to complete assignments', a disclosure rule, P24 (the documentation-of-process aspect also touches P26).

units.why: Students 'are encouraged to learn to use AI tools in ways that support their success', a welcoming stance bounded by university guidelines, P02.
units.anchor: Students are encouraged to learn to use AI tools in ways that support their success
units.fit_note: Encouragement is bounded by university guidelines and academic integrity.

units.why: Students 'are responsible to know, understand, and comply with AI guidelines established for their courses', P78.

units.fit_note: Permission depends on teacher direction and covers learning, thinking and creativity, not only tutoring.

units.why: Students are to 'Document the use of AI as directed by their teachers', a disclosure duty set by the teacher, P24.
units.anchor: Document the use of AI as directed by their teachers when completing assignments.

units.why: Students may 'Share their own experiences and skills with emerging technologies with teachers and peers'. A community-sharing item; closest is P66.
units.anchor: Share their own experiences and skills with emerging technologies with teachers and peers.
units.fit_note: Student-side sharing rather than instructors explaining rules.

units.why: 'By submitting any academic work, students ... attest that they have adhered to all established requirements', an attestation duty, P29.

units.why: Where AI material is allowed, users attest 'all sources used ... that go beyond common knowledge, are attributed', a citation duty, P24.

units.why: Users attest 'That generated material accurately reflects the facts', a duty to verify AI output, P31.

units.why: Untrue attestations 'whether by intent or negligence' are 'deceit' and 'academic misconduct', reviewed under the Academic Integrity Code, P36.

units.why: 'AI systems should be approved for use by a UAB vetting counsel' with legal, compliance, finance, IT and faculty members: review and approval of tools, P65.

units.why: The goal is to 'choose secure, useful, and cost-effective tools with minimal overlap in functionality', a tool-selection criterion, P65.

units.why: It recommends privacy safeguards since 'personal data collected or processed by ChatGPT ... becomes part of the product', P50. It is aimed at the legal office, not at users.

units.why: It says 'ChatGPT interfaces should comply with accessibility standards and guidelines such as WCAG 2.1 or 2.2', an accessibility requirement, P97.

notes: The CTL page largely repeats the provost report samples; each document was coded on its own. The report covers clinical and research topics; only education-relevant policy and rationale were coded, and the descriptive 'Potential Impact' bullets were coded selectively (integrity, equity, skills, bias, IP).
